minutes.headline: Sewer Commission approved twice-yearly grease trap cleaning at three schools and backdated a $25-a-day fine for a non-compliant site.
minutes.summary: The commission heard a waiver request to cut grease trap cleanings at the middle-high school, primary school and Turkey Hill from three times a year to twice. Members argued over a possible design flaw in the dishwasher rinse plumbing and a tilted pipe on the external interceptor. The waivers were moved and carried without conditions. The commission also discussed an engineering evaluation scope, a sub-metering policy, legal fees, a grease trap compliance penalty and the minutes.

what_happened.line: The Sewer Commission voted to grant grease trap waivers at the middle-high school, primary school and Turkey Hill, cutting cleanings from three a year to two.
The external tank at the middle-high school moves to once a year; a contingency attached to that was later dropped.
A motion to apply the daily non-compliance fee retroactively from July 2018 was made, but the outcome is not audible in the recording.
Karl is to bring two or three engineering firms to the next meeting to discuss the scope of the system evaluation.
Counsel is to advise on a sub-metering policy before the commission decides how to approach the park owner.

why_it_matters: Fewer grease trap cleanings lower what the schools pay for maintenance, but members raised a possible plumbing design flaw, so less frequent cleaning carries a risk of blockages in the sewer system.
The engineering evaluation, the sub-metering policy and the legal fee arrangement bear on how sewer costs are measured and shared among users, which feeds into sewer rates.
